questions.stem: For an ideal Bose gas in three dimensions, the condensation temperature \(T_c\) depends on number density \(n\) as:

explanation.howToModify: Ask how \(T_c\) changes if the density is multiplied by 8 (×4).

questions.stem: For an ideal 3D Bose gas, the condensate fraction is \(N_0/N = 1-(T/T_c)^{3/2}\). At \(T = T_c/2\) it is about:

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the temperature at which half the atoms are condensed (\(T = 0.63T_c\)).
explanation.howToAvoid: Compute the power carefully and subtract from 1.

questions.stem: For a uniform ideal Bose gas (no trap), Bose–Einstein condensation at non-zero temperature:

options.B: occurs in 3D but not in 1D or 2D

explanation.whyCorrect: The excited-state integral \(\int g(\varepsilon)/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)d\varepsilon\) with \(\mu = 0\) converges only if \(g(\varepsilon)\) rises fast enough; with \(g\propto\varepsilon^{d/2-1}\) it diverges for \(d\le2\), so excited states can absorb all particles.

whyWrong.A: Lower dimensions fail for the uniform gas.

explanation.howToModify: Ask whether BEC is possible in a 2D harmonic trap (yes — the density of states changes).
explanation.howToAvoid: Check convergence of the integral near ε = 0.

questions.stem: Bose–Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic gas was first achieved in 1995 using:

explanation.whyCorrect: Cornell and Wieman condensed \(^{87}\)Rb; Ketterle achieved BEC in sodium shortly after (Nobel Prize 2001).

whyWrong.A: Photons in a cavity have μ = 0 and no conserved number (photon BEC came only in 2010 with special dye cavities).
whyWrong.B: \(^3\)He atoms are fermions (superfluidity arises via pairing).

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the approximate temperature (≈ 170 nK).

questions.stem: The onset of Bose–Einstein condensation in a uniform 3D ideal gas occurs when the phase-space density \(n\lambda_T^3\) reaches about:

explanation.whyCorrect: Condensation begins at \(n\lambda_T^3 = \zeta(3/2)\approx2.612\): thermal wave packets overlap.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for \(\lambda_T\) of Rb at 100 nK.

questions.stem: Liquid \(^4\)He becomes superfluid below the lambda point at approximately:

explanation.whyCorrect: The \(\lambda\)-transition at 2.17 K (named after the shape of \(C_P(T)\)) is linked to BEC of the interacting bosonic \(^4\)He atoms; ideal-gas estimate gives ≈ 3.1 K.
explanation.trapUsed: Confusing boiling point with the lambda point.
explanation.howToModify: Ask why \(^3\)He requires much lower temperatures (Cooper pairing of fermions).
explanation.howToAvoid: Associate 4.2 K with boiling and 2.17 K with superfluidity.
